boundaries.contract: `cmd_Protocol` is a `ConfCmdFn` stored as `SslConfCmdTbl.cmd` by the private `commands()` table (`src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:835`, row `:911`). The only indirect invocation is `f(cctx, value)` in `SSL_CONF_cmd` (`:1318`), reached from `SSL_CONF_cmd_argv` (`:1336` -> `:1382`). `SSL_CONF_cmd_value_type` (`:1409`) reads only `value_type`, never `.cmd`. Preconditions: (1) `cctx` is non-NULL, aligned, live, initialised, and exclusively accessible: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects a NULL `cctx`/`cmd` at `:1290`; provenance is one zeroed `size_of::<SslConfCtx>()` block from `SSL_CONF_CTX_new` (`:1438`); `SSL_CONF_CTX_set_ssl`/`_set_ssl_ctx` (`:1561`/`:1605`) set `ctx`/`ssl` to NULL or live in-crate objects; the shared `&*cctx` at `:1302` is used only for lookup and ends (NLL) before `:1318`, so the handler's writes do not alias a live shared borrow. (2) `value` is non-NULL and NUL-terminated: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects NULL for a typed row at `:1311`; NUL-termination is the public caller contract at `:1281`. (3) No retention of `value`: the handler passes it to `parse_option_list`, which stores only the frame-local flag table in `cctx.tbl` and clears `tbl`/`ntbl` before returning (`:407-434`). (4) Return: `CONF_parse_list` gives 1 when an element matched and 0 otherwise; `SSL_CONF_cmd` maps >0 to 2 and every other value to 0. (5) NULL `cctx` is never delivered (dispatch guard); if it were, the handler would dereference it. A NULL `value` is not delivered either; the handler would answer 0 (CONF_parse_list's NULL arm). (6) Error path: `cctx.tbl`/`ntbl` are cleared on every path; `CONF_parse_list` has its own `guard_ffi`. Only the slot being private and the exclusivity of the C caller are authority-derived (see preconditions).

negative_control.name: ssl::ssl_conf::tests::conf_cmd_dispatch_feeds_a_live_ctx_and_does_not_retain_the_value
negative_control.observation: SSL_CONF_cmd('Options','Bugs') returns 2, sets SSL_OP_ALL in the live option word, and clears cctx.tbl; a second call with '-Bugs' independently clears the bit; a NULL value is refused with -3 and changes no state; a direct cmd_Options(NULL) returns -3. Together these show the callback receives a live SslConfCtx and a NUL-terminated value through the .cmd slot, retains neither, and that a NULL value is handled.
negative_control.fails_if: the cmd_Options NULL guard is removed: observed left 0 / right -3 at src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:1759 (see evidence.mutation)
negative_control.limits: The test does not exercise a real SSL/SSL_CTX for every handler; the cipher/protocol handlers are covered only through the shared dispatch/table-clearing path and their static contracts. It does not prove NUL-termination of an arbitrary caller buffer (that is the caller's contract), only that the handler consumes the literal up to its terminator.
